newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Germany, Austria say will stick to EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Germany, Austria say will stick to EMU criteria.

text.p: The German and Austrian governments reiterated on Sunday their firm determination to stick to the Maastricht criteria for Europe's planned economic and monetary union (EMU).

In a joint statement released after an informal meeting of the country's foreign ministers in the western Austrian ski resort of Lech am Arlberg, they said: "We reaffirm our conviction to call for full compliance with all criteria for joining economic and monetary union."
Countries wanting to join EMU -- scheduled to begin in 1999 -- face strict entry criteria in terms of public deficits, debt levels, inflation and exchange rate stability.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and his Austrian counterpart Wolfgang Schuessel said the single currency, the euro, was the "biggest challenge" for Europe over the coming years.
Kinkel earlier on Sunday attacked what he called "irresponsible" market speculation that Germany was seeking a delay of EMU, saying the launch of the euro was a "question of fate" for Europe.

Speculation that Germany may seek a delay of the project because it may not meet all the entry criteria deeply unsettled world financial markets on Friday. The rumours were denied both by the Bundesbank and the German finance ministry.
